title: Man ran at officer, eyewitnesses agree
article: The young man shot dead by Port Moody police was running at an officer with a machete when he was struck down.
Const. Brian Soles said statements taken from the two eyewitnesses at the scene early Monday support the police version of events.
"The deceased ran at the police officer with an upraised machete," Soles said yesterday. "They both agreed that that was the case."
The dead youth was named as Keyvan Tabesh, 18, of Burnaby. He was shot a number of times by a plainclothes officer early Monday morning.
Police said Tabesh was prohibited from driving, but was behind the wheel of his black Honda Prelude with two male friends from Coquitlam.
Earlier that night, Tabesh attacked a red Dodge Shadow with a machete, after bumping it with his car.
While the two female occupants, both in their 20s, were inside, Tabesh "went nuts on the car."
As police took the women's statements, the Prelude passed by.
The 20-year veteran officer responded to the investigating officers' call, and pursued the car down a dead-end.

Tabesh and one youth got out and approached the officer, who fired at both men. Tabesh died in a hail of bullets, while the other man is expected to be released from hospital after non-life- threatening injuries.
"Somebody made a mistake that night," said Soles. "It was them."
He said there were lots of ways out at the end of the cul-de- sac.
"These people did not have their backs to the wall. If they wanted to get away from police, they had ample avenues available to them."
Police say Tabesh came to Canada from the Middle East two years ago.
He dropped out of Burnaby North Secondary School in the middle of last year.
He also attended Gleneagle Secondary School in Coquitlam, where it is believed he befriended the two young men who were the passengers.

While he has no criminal charges or convictions against him, Soles said he has had "contact" with police in the past. It will be up the B.C.'s Chief Coroner to decide whether to hold a coroner's inquest into the death.
The officer is on sick leave, pending an internal investigation.
